job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

passage: Today in our science lab, we explored how our bodies process iron. We learned that iron is a vital mineral that helps haemoglobin carry oxygen to all our cells. Contrary to what some believe, iron does not exist as rust particles in our blood; it is a complex part of the haemoglobin molecule itself. We also discussed that anaemia is not a contagious disease that spreads through contact, nor does it mean a person has 'less blood' in their body. Instead, anaemia occurs when there is not enough healthy haemoglobin to transport oxygen effectively. During our discussion, we looked at how we absorb iron. Even if we eat iron-rich foods like spinach or lentils, our bodies do not absorb all of it automatically. We discovered that Vitamin C helps our bodies absorb iron, but it does not provide the iron itself. Furthermore, we learned that while milk is nutritious, it is not a complete food for preventing anaemia because it lacks sufficient iron. Finally, we clarified that iron tablets are supplements to be taken alongside a balanced diet, not replacements for iron-rich meals. Maintaining healthy levels of iron is about balance, as consuming excessive amounts of iron supplements without medical advice can be harmful to our health.

items.evidence: Instead, anaemia occurs when there is not enough healthy haemoglobin to transport oxygen effectively.
items.q: Meena has plenty of blood but is often tired. Which could explain anaemia?
options: Her blood lacks enough healthy haemoglobin
Her body makes too little blood overall
Her blood has no white blood cells
She caught it from a classmate
items.explain: Anaemia means too little healthy haemoglobin to carry oxygen, not too little blood.

wrong.why: thinks anaemia means too little blood
thinks anaemia means no white blood cells
thinks anaemia spreads like a cold

items.evidence: We discovered that Vitamin C helps our bodies absorb iron, but it does not provide the iron itself.
items.q: Hari drinks lemon juice with his lentil meal. What does the lemon juice do?
options: It helps his body take in the iron
It adds extra iron to the meal
It turns the lentils into haemoglobin
It gives his body energy to move
items.explain: Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron but does not supply iron itself.

wrong.why: thinks Vitamin C contains the iron
thinks food turns straight into haemoglobin

items.evidence: Even if we eat iron-rich foods like spinach or lentils, our bodies do not absorb all of it automatically.
items.q: Asha eats spinach daily but still has low iron. Which is a likely reason?
options: Her body absorbs only part of the iron
Spinach has no iron to give her
One spinach meal should have cured her
Only meat and eggs can give iron
items.explain: Bodies do not absorb all the iron in food, so eating iron-rich food does not guarantee enough iron.

wrong.why: thinks spinach cures anaemia at once
thinks only meat and eggs have iron

items.evidence: Furthermore, we learned that while milk is nutritious, it is not a complete food for preventing anaemia because it lacks sufficient iron.
items.q: Why can milk alone not protect a child from anaemia?
options: It does not have enough iron
It blocks the body from taking in iron
It has too much iron for the body
It is not liked by most children
items.explain: Milk is nutritious but lacks sufficient iron, so it cannot fully prevent anaemia by itself.

wrong.why: thinks milk is a complete food for iron
thinks extra iron is always good
picks a nearby idea not given in the passage

items.evidence: Maintaining healthy levels of iron is about balance, as consuming excessive amounts of iron supplements without medical advice can be harmful to our health.
items.q: Ravi takes many iron tablets daily, thinking more iron is always better. What is true?
options: Too much iron can harm his health
He will become healthier each day
He no longer needs iron-rich meals
He will be cured of anaemia sooner
items.explain: Taking too many iron supplements without medical advice can harm health; balance matters.

wrong.why: thinks more iron is always healthier
thinks a larger dose cures faster
